devices._comment: One entry per device. password_env names an environment variable to read the password from at runtime — never put a plaintext password in this file. port/timeout_seconds/fast_cli/global_delay_factor are optional (defaults shown here). If you see a Netmiko 'Pattern not detected' error, the device is slower to respond than expected (common for a device reached over the public internet rather than a LAN) — raise BOTH timeout_seconds (e.g. 60) and global_delay_factor (e.g. 2) for that device; timeout_seconds alone only covers the initial connection and each command's read timeout, not Netmiko's internal pattern-detection delays that global_delay_factor scales.

detection_rules._comment: Toggle individual rules on/off without editing rules.json. A rule id absent from this map defaults to enabled.

expected_local_users._comment: Baseline allow-list for the unauthorized-local-accounts rule. Any 'username <x>' line in running-config not in this list is flagged per device (device_overrides can extend/replace the global list for one host).

ai._comment: Forensicator AI is OFF by default. Set enabled=true and point base_url/model at a local LLM (e.g. Ollama) or a commercial API to get a per-finding verdict written into each finding's ai_analysis field, shown in reports/index.html and printed to the console as each finding is analyzed. Same provider/config shape as the Windows/Linux/macOS collectors: provider: ollama | openai | openai_compatible | azure_openai | anthropic. api_key is only needed for openai/openai_compatible/azure_openai/anthropic. max_evidence_rows caps how much of a large finding's evidence (e.g. a full running-config) is actually sent to the LLM per call.
